ai.description: Lycodon zawi is a slender snake reaching 60 cm. It is dark brown with thin, pale yellow crossbands and a distinct white V-shaped mark on the nape. It features a flattened head and smooth scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lycodon zawi* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of narrow, white, widely spaced cross-bars that do not reach the belly, unlike the broader bands of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Lycodon zawi* inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at low to moderate elevations within dense, humid vegetation.
ai.behavior: Lycodon zawi is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours foraging for small lizards and frogs among the leaf litter and rocky crevices of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon zawi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in Northeast India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon zawi* is endemic to the Mizoram state in Northeast India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forests within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
